anomalies.observed: Net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW connects only to D14 pin 2 (anode), D23 pin 2 (anode), and D4 pin 1 (cathode). It has no connection to any supply rail or driver.
anomalies.expected: The net should be connected to a 3.3V supply (e.g., +3V3) to power the Ethernet LEDs D14/D23 and LED D4.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet activity LEDs D14 and D23, and the green LED D4, will never illuminate because their anodes/cathodes have no current path to a supply.

anomalies.observed: R60 pin 2 is on ESTOP_OUT, and D30 pin 4 (A2) is also on ESTOP_OUT. R60 pin 1 connects to D30 pin 2 (K2). Thus the second LED of D30 has its anode and cathode both tied to ESTOP_OUT (one directly, one through R60).
anomalies.expected: R60 should connect D30 K2 to GND (or the LED should be wired between +3V3 and ESTOP_OUT) so that the LED can indicate the e-stop state.
anomalies.impact: The e-stop indicator LED (second LED of D30) is shorted and will never light, removing visual feedback for the e-stop signal.

anomalies.observed: The isolated-side ground pins GND2 of the isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 are tied directly to the common GND net.
anomalies.expected: For isolated CAN buses, the isolated-side ground (GND2) must be separate from the logic-side ground (GND1) and connected only to an isolated ground net.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: The galvanic isolation of the CAN buses is defeated because the isolated side is referenced to the same ground as the logic side, eliminating the intended isolation barrier.

parsed.summary: The design files contain multiple anomalies: a floating LED power net (/LED_3.3V_POWER_SW) that disables Ethernet and status LEDs, a miswired e-stop indicator LED (R60 to ESTOP_OUT instead of GND), and isolated CAN transceivers whose isolated grounds are tied to common GND, defeating the specified isolation.
